directorStatement.audienceFeeling: The audience is inside Bo’s private delay ritual as it turns from cosy play into a little panic machine, then feels the room open when Keen sees the feared tail and answers with wonder instead of alarm.
directorStatement.emotionalChange: Bo owns the scene until Keen reframes him. The camera’s sympathy stays with Bo’s Want — keep the day small, keep the tail unseen, keep the decision reversible — while quietly exposing his Need: one kind witness who does not treat the tail as a disaster. Keen is not staged as the solution; he is the first presence that makes staying visible survivable.
directorStatement.theLaugh: The governing mechanism is environmental participation: the conker, satchel, doorway light, Mum’s offscreen call and Bo’s tail all become players in his argument with today. The comedy escalates through overcommitment: Bo tries to make one tiny object decide a giant life question, and the more seriously he treats the conker, the more obvious his panic becomes. The dramatic turn is Keen’s sincere awe at the tail, which converts private shame into shared wonder without explaining it.
directorStatement.visualSurprise: Bo inside the hollow oak with the lunch satchel and conker close at hand, the open doorway waiting in brighter depth like a question he is trying not to answer. -> Bo and Keen moving toward the same doorway together, the conker left behind in the warm room, the outside light now reading as fresh air rather than exposure.
directorStatement.carryForward: Bo and Keen leave the room together for fresh air; Bo’s worry is not solved, but being seen has become survivable enough to move.

northStar.surfaceStory: Bo tries to delay leaving his hollow oak for the Learning Circle, gets caught in a conker-and-door panic loop, then Keen arrives, sees the feared tail “thing,” and helps Bo take one small step out for a walk.
northStar.universalTruth: Sometimes the part of yourself you are trying hardest to hide is the part someone kind sees first — and they do not flinch.
northStar.childClearWant: Bo wants to not go today because he is scared nobody will like him if his tail acts funny.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Bo needs one safe witness who reacts with delight instead of alarm, so leaving the room can feel possible without pretending the fear is gone.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If my tail does the thing where people can see it, I won’t belong.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Keen changes the room by being gently present rather than clever: he arrives at the doorway, does not laugh at Bo, looks at the tail with wonder, then makes his own tail the joke so Bo no longer has to be the joke.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A child can rehearse bravery alone forever; often the first real movement happens only when another person stands nearby and makes being seen feel less dangerous.
northStar.sceneTurn: The turn lands when Bo’s tail does exactly what he feared and Keen answers it with sincere awe — “Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING.” Bo’s shame does not disappear, but it loses enough grip for curiosity to enter.
audienceJourney: Safe, cosy delay: the child recognises the “one more minute” stall.
Comic worry: the conker loop makes panic playable and visible.
Startle: Keen’s knock exposes Bo’s private rehearsal.
Little gasp: the tail does the dreaded thing in front of someone new.
Relief-laugh: Keen’s useless-tail demonstration redirects embarrassment into shared silliness.
Forward warmth: leaving for a walk feels like a first step, not a solved problem.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: A small brave exhale: Bo is not ready for everything, but he is no longer alone inside the doorway.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any explanation of Bo’s fear or Keen’s kindness beyond the locked lines. The conker-in/conker-out loop, Bo’s retreat from the open door, the tail’s visible betrayal, Keen’s wonder-filled look, and the useless-tail demonstration should carry the meaning without extra dialogue.
northStar.environmentPressure: The hollow oak is warm and protective, but the open doorway, Mum’s offscreen call, the lunch satchel, outside daylight, and the visible path to the Learning Circle all press Bo toward leaving. The conker turns the room into a little decision machine: each roll toward or away from the door physically restarts the argument in Bo’s body.

transformation.entryBelief: If I wait a little longer and keep checking, I can avoid today and keep my tail from ruining things.
transformation.entryFeeling: Cosy but trapped; comfort is turning into panic because the safe room also proves he has not left.
transformation.pressureBehaviour: He answers Mum with delay, negotiates with the conker and satchel, reaches the door, freezes, retreats, and repeats the conker choice until the loop becomes panic.
transformation.costlyChoice: When Keen sees the tail do the thing, Bo does not slam the door or fully hide; he stays present long enough to hear Keen’s wonder and then accepts the walk.
transformation.exitBelief: Maybe being seen by one kind someone is survivable; maybe my tail is not only a problem.
transformation.exitAction: Bo leaves the hollow oak with Keen for fresh air, carrying the fear forward instead of resolving it inside the room.

tapestry.physicalMotif: The conker is Bo’s decision switch: in, out, in, out — a tiny object doing the work of a giant worry. The tail is the uncontrolled truth that interrupts the switch and forces the real fear into the room.
tapestry.sonicMotif: Keep the hollow quiet enough that small sounds feel huge: Mum’s offscreen call, satchel rustle, conker taps, the open-door hush, Keen’s gentle knock, then the soft comic beat of Keen demonstrating his tail doing nothing. Silence should widen just before and just after the tail ‘thing.’
tapestry.colourAndLightProgression: Begin in honeyed, enclosed warmth inside the hollow oak, with the doorway carrying brighter outside light that feels too big. As Keen enters, let the threshold light become less threatening and more shared; by the exit, the same daylight reads as fresh air rather than exposure.
tapestry.thematicVisualContrast: Private loop versus shared movement: Bo alone circling objects in a safe room, then Bo and Keen oriented toward the same doorway. Also controlled small conker versus uncontrollable large tail — the thing Bo can manage versus the thing he cannot.
tapestry.openingClosingRhyme: Opening image: Bo inside the hollow, clutching the mechanics of delay while the door waits. Closing image: Bo crossing toward that same door with Keen beside him. The doorway changes meaning from test to invitation, while the worry remains visible enough to preserve the episode’s larger journey.

creativeIntent.selectedTreatment: Treatment 1 — The Room That Keeps Saying “Not Yet,” strengthened by Treatment 2’s tail-as-truth emphasis and Treatment 3’s threshold logic
creativeIntent.governingAudienceExperience: The audience is inside Bo’s private delay ritual as it turns from cosy play into a little panic machine, then feels the room open when Keen sees the feared tail and answers with wonder instead of alarm.
creativeIntent.scenePurpose: Bo’s private delaying ritual turns from cosy control into exposed panic, then Keen’s gentle witnessing makes one small step toward the doorway possible.
creativeIntent.emotionalPointOfView: Bo owns the scene until Keen reframes him. The camera’s sympathy stays with Bo’s Want — keep the day small, keep the tail unseen, keep the decision reversible — while quietly exposing his Need: one kind witness who does not treat the tail as a disaster. Keen is not staged as the solution; he is the first presence that makes staying visible survivable.
creativeIntent.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The governing mechanism is environmental participation: the conker, satchel, doorway light, Mum’s offscreen call and Bo’s tail all become players in his argument with today. The comedy escalates through overcommitment: Bo tries to make one tiny object decide a giant life question, and the more seriously he treats the conker, the more obvious his panic becomes. The dramatic turn is Keen’s sincere awe at the tail, which converts private shame into shared wonder without explaining it.
creativeIntent.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo’s acting is small-choice panic: paws hover, commit, retract; his attention ricochets from conker to satchel to open door to tail. His body keeps trying to be tidy while his tail tells the truth bigger than he can. He does not perform “fear” broadly; he performs control failing. Keen enters with gentle curiosity: he knocks like he knows a room can be startled, then keeps his body soft and available. When he demonstrates his own tail doing nothing, he makes himself the silly object on purpose — not clowning for attention, but offering Bo somewhere safe to laugh.
creativeIntent.visualGrammar: The hollow oak begins as a warm circular enclosure, all curved surfaces and reachable objects, but the open door is a bright vertical interruption that feels too large for Bo’s current courage. Composition should make the room feel like it is looping: Bo repeatedly returns to the same decision objects, but each return is less cosy and more cornered. Once Keen appears, the visual grammar shifts from circles to shared lines toward the doorway. The door does not get brighter; Bo’s relationship to it changes.
creativeIntent.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like Bo’s worry: close to the objects he can control, hesitant near the threshold, easily startled by interruption. It may discover Keen only when Bo does, because the shock is part of Bo’s experience. After Keen’s wonder at the tail, the camera stops acting like a hiding place and becomes a witness that can hold both embarrassment and kindness in the same emotional space.
creativeIntent.movementVersusStillness: Before Keen, motion is repetitive and fussy: conker in, conker out, satchel touch, door approach, retreat. Stillness arrives only as freeze — the body trapped. Keen introduces a different stillness: calm attention. The tail’s sudden uncontrolled action is the biggest movement in the scene, and Keen’s still, delighted look is what changes its meaning. At the end, Bo and Keen’s shared movement out should be modest, not triumphant: one small walk, not a victory parade.
creativeIntent.depthAndEnvironment: Use depth as pressure. The foreground holds Bo’s manageable objects; the mid-ground holds Bo; the background doorway holds the day he is avoiding. Mum’s voice comes from beyond the room but never needs a body; the outside world is present as sound and light. When Keen arrives, he occupies the threshold without conquering it, turning the doorway from a boundary into a meeting place. The conker should travel through the room in a way that lets the audience always understand where the door is relative to Bo.
creativeIntent.rhythmAndEscalation: Start with soft domestic tempo, then let the conker loop create comic meter: decision, reversal, decision, reversal. Each spoken line from Bo should land as another attempt to negotiate with time, not as exposition. The panic peak is not loudness alone; it is the moment the loop can no longer contain the tail. Keen’s “Whoa” must slow the rhythm sharply — the scene inhales — then the useless-tail demonstration releases the tension quickly into a gentle laugh.
creativeIntent.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by decision changes, not coverage. Cut when the conker changes the argument, when the doorway becomes too big, when Keen’s presence changes the privacy of the room, and when Bo’s tail forces the real fear into view. Avoid automatic reaction cutting; sometimes the funniest or truest reaction is letting Bo and the object share the frame until the audience feels how seriously he is taking it. Hold briefly after Keen’s awe so Bo’s shame has time to become curiosity.
creativeIntent.openingImage: Bo inside the hollow oak with the lunch satchel and conker close at hand, the open doorway waiting in brighter depth like a question he is trying not to answer.
creativeIntent.closingImage: Bo and Keen moving toward the same doorway together, the conker left behind in the warm room, the outside light now reading as fresh air rather than exposure.
creativeIntent.handoverToNextScene: Bo and Keen leave the room together for fresh air; Bo’s worry is not solved, but being seen has become survivable enough to move.
creativeIntent.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, lightly funny relief: the room should feel that Bo did not become a different squirrel; he became seen, and the honeycomb button lets the audience leave laughing without erasing the cost of the day.

emotion.entryState: Comforted by the warm hollow and the nearby lunch satchel and conker.
emotion.pressure: Mum’s offscreen call, the Learning Circle, the lunch reminder and the open doorway all ask for forward motion now.
emotion.choiceOrRealisation: Bo chooses delay instead of departure, keeping the decision small enough to handle by touching objects in the room.
emotion.exitState: Still safe, but more trapped; the room now contains proof that he has not gone.
emotion.observableEvidence: His attention ricochets between conker, satchel and door; his paws hover and retract before his line promises only a minute.

comedy.setup: Mum asks from outside that it is time to go and reminds him about lunch.
comedy.expectation: Bo will collect the satchel and leave.
comedy.disruption: Bo treats the nearby objects as if they can negotiate the morning for him.
comedy.button: His line makes delay sound tiny even as the room shows the size of what he is avoiding.
comedy.hold: Let the satchel, conker and open doorway share the emotional space long enough for the audience to feel how seriously Bo is outsourcing the decision.

emotion.entryState: Trying to make leaving feel manageable by reducing it to one object and one doorway.
emotion.pressure: The open door confronts him with the outside day, and each conker choice fails to settle the fear.
emotion.choiceOrRealisation: Bo chooses to keep restarting the decision instead of accepting any one answer.
emotion.exitState: Cornered by his own ritual; the panic is now louder than the cosy delay.
emotion.observableEvidence: He freezes at the threshold, retreats, repeats the conker action, and his final line breaks the earlier negotiation rhythm.
emotion.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds both the laugh of the conker loop and the ache that Bo cannot get out by deciding harder.

comedy.setup: Bo uses a conker as the physical switch for whether today can happen.
comedy.expectation: One clear conker choice will settle the argument and let him move.
comedy.disruption: Every choice creates the opposite choice; the more seriously Bo obeys the conker, the less control he has.
comedy.hold: Hold the final conker position with Bo’s panic still attached to it so the audience catches the absurd size of the job he has given the object.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: The conker, Bo’s paws, the lunch satchel and the open doorway remain readable in relation to one another so the audience tracks the decision loop and the pressure of the exit.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Each conker move has small tactile weight: paw pads gather it, set it down or pull it back; the satchel shifts only when Bo actually touches or bumps it, proving the room is responding to his fussy momentum.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A repeated in-out pattern tightens into faster, less tidy reversals until Bo’s body freezes and the final line pops out as the ritual fails him.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the conker into a magical chooser or animated character.
Do not make the loop so fast that the audience loses where the doorway is.
Do not cut away from the conker’s final position before Bo’s panic lands.

emotion.entryState: Overwound inside the conker loop, focused on controlling the next tiny decision.
emotion.pressure: A new bear appears exactly where the day has been pressing in: the open doorway.
emotion.choiceOrRealisation: Bo does not shut the encounter down immediately; despite the startle, he remains in the room with Keen present.
emotion.exitState: Exposed and startled, but not invaded; Keen’s softness keeps the threshold from becoming an attack.
emotion.observableEvidence: The conker flies from Bo’s startle, while Keen stays at the doorway with simple, friendly lines rather than pushing deeper into the room.
emotion.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds the relief that Keen is gentle and the tension that Bo’s real fear is about to surface.

comedy.setup: Bo’s whole body is locked into the conker’s private decision ritual.
comedy.expectation: The next movement will be another controlled conker choice.
comedy.disruption: A friendly knock turns control into a startled launch.
comedy.button: Keen’s calm introduction lands against Bo’s oversized startle.
comedy.hold: Keep a brief beat on the contrast between the flown conker and Keen’s soft doorway presence so the laugh does not make Keen feel careless.

emotion.entryState: Socially exposed and trying to explain why the Learning Circle feels impossible.
emotion.pressure: His feared tail behaviour happens immediately in front of the new witness.
emotion.choiceOrRealisation: Bo stays present long enough to hear Keen’s wonder instead of fully hiding or ending the encounter.
emotion.exitState: Unsure but newly curious; the tail may not only be a problem if someone can see it with delight.
emotion.observableEvidence: Bo blurts the fear, pleads with his tail, then softens into the small, disbelieving question after Keen’s line.
emotion.heldAfterBeat: Keen’s awe remains in the room as a new possible meaning for the tail, but Bo’s fear is still visible.

comedy.setup: Bo fears his tail will do the thing where others can see it.
comedy.expectation: The tail’s action will confirm disaster and make Bo the joke.
comedy.disruption: The tail does act out, but Keen receives it as amazing rather than ridiculous.
comedy.hold: Hold briefly after Keen’s awe so Bo’s shame has time to become curiosity; do not rush into the next gag.

emotion.entryState: Fragile curiosity after Keen’s awe, still carrying embarrassment and uncertainty.
emotion.pressure: The doorway and Learning Circle remain ahead, and Bo must choose whether to stay inside or move with Keen.
emotion.choiceOrRealisation: Bo accepts a small walk as the next step, not as a promise that everything is fixed.
emotion.exitState: Warmer and braver by one notch; fear travels with him, but so does a kind witness.
emotion.observableEvidence: His tail softens, his smile grows, and he answers Keen’s invitation before moving toward the same doorway with him.
emotion.heldAfterBeat: The conker remains behind as a trace of the old loop, while Bo carries a small brave exhale into the next scene.

comedy.mechanism: Hiding failure turned into generous self-joke
comedy.setup: Bo’s tail has just been treated as amazing, but Bo is still unsure what to do with being seen.
comedy.expectation: Keen might explain, reassure too much, or make Bo’s tail the continued focus.
comedy.disruption: Keen makes his own tail the intentionally useless comparison, moving the joke onto himself.
comedy.hold: Let Bo register that Keen is offering silliness, not judgement, before the invitation to walk redirects the scene toward the doorway.

shots.purpose: Establish Bo’s Want as delay and the room’s pressure as active without explaining the fear yet.
shots.performanceAssignment: Performance phases: anticipation: ENVIRONMENT Warm hollow surfaces hold Bo close while the bright open doorway remains visible behind him as a vertical interruption; action: Bo Bo’s paws hover near the satchel, pull back, and return toward the conker as his eyeline flicks from object to doorway and back; reaction: Bo After the offscreen prompt, Bo keeps his body low and tidy instead of rising toward the threshold; settle: Bo Bo remains beside the satchel and conker, angled inward, with the open doorway still unanswered behind him. Cause and effect: The offscreen household call makes the doorway active; Bo’s eyeline checks it, but his hands choose the satchel and conker, so his body stays inside and the threshold remains uncrossed. Visible turn: Bo shifts from resting in a safe room to using the room’s objects to delay movement. Land on: Bo must end visibly inside the hollow, close to the conker and satchel, with the doorway still waiting in depth. Acting freedom: Allow variation in blink cadence, paw tremble, tail settling, and the exact size of each hesitation, as long as Bo never appears ready to stride out.
shots.camera: Start low inside the hollow across the conker and satchel toward Bo, keep the open doorway readable in bright depth, and let Bo’s small paw hesitations carry the delay as Mum’s offscreen call turns the room into a question.
shots.openingPose: Bo inside the hollow oak beside the lunch satchel and conker, with the open doorway brighter behind him like an unanswered question.
shots.cutInMotivation: A cut is stronger than remaining continuous because the next unit begins a new causal engine: Bo physically tests the doorway and the conker loop starts making decisions for him. Holding one flow would blur the shift from cosy delay to repeated panic ritual.

inputs.title: The Tail Thing
inputs.logline: When small squirrel Bo cannot get himself out the door for his first visit to the Learning Circle, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very tail he wants to hide may be the thing that helps him belong.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen stages a tiny, over-careful honey heist in the golden meadow, but every crunch and Fuzzby’s sleeping presence turns the sneaking into comic suspense. The beat is about Keen wanting the prize without being seen, while the world makes invisibility impossible.

beats.need: He needs to learn that being clever and quiet is not the same as being ready for what the world does back.
beats.kidRead: A funny sneaking game where every little sound could wake the bee.
beats.adultRead: A child trying to control every variable, unaware that bodies and worlds never behave perfectly.
beats.emotionalIntent: Playful tension: giggles held in the body, with the audience leaning toward the honeycomb.
